description: Track users who own numbered chunks on a shared server. Example 1: users join owning [1, 2] and [2, 3]; a request for chunk 2 returns both owners in ascending user-ID order. Example 2: after the first user leaves, its chunks have no owners until another user uploads or requests them. Constraints: chunk IDs lie in the server's fixed range, users receive reusable positive IDs, and request results are sorted.
intuition: Both directions of the ownership relation are needed: a user must release all its chunks, and a chunk request must list all owners.

brute_force.approach: Store each user's chunks and scan all users whenever a chunk owner list is requested.
brute_force.time: join O(chunks), leave O(chunks + users), request O(users)

optimal.approach: Maintain user-to-chunk and chunk-to-user sets, plus a min-heap of reusable user IDs.
optimal.time: join O(chunks + log users), leave O(chunks + log users), request O(owners log owners)

edge_cases: A user requesting an already-owned chunk does not duplicate ownership.
A request returns current owners before adding the requester.
